newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Astra posts mixed first-half results.
newsitem.headline: Astra posts mixed first-half results.

text.p: Swedish drug company Astra AB posted a disappointing 4 percent rise in first-half pretax profit Friday, disappointing investors and analysts.
While the company sought to reassure investors by saying growth should pick up again next year, analysts said they were concerned about Astra's prospects as its key anti-ulcer drug Losec matures.
Astra's shares fell 5 percent on the Stockholm Stock Exchange after the news.

The company posted a 13 percent rise in sales to 21.47 billion crowns ($2.7 billion), in line with expectations. But the 4 percent increase in pretax profits to 7.01 billion crowns ($882 million) was below market forecasts of 7.18 billion ($904 million).
Chief Executive Hakan Mogren tried to put a positive spin on the results, saying the future looked brighter.
"Growth is leveling off somewhat but will pick up later," Mogren told a news conference. "We are on our way to getting approval for a number of significant products."
Sales of Losec -- its largest product, which will see its patent expire in 2001 -- rose to 14.72 billion crowns ($1.85 billion) worldwide from 11.78 billion crowns ($1.48 billion).

Astra's own sales of Losec in the United States, where it jointly markets the drug with Merck & Co. Inc. as Prilosec, rose to 10.12 billion crowns ($1.27 billion) from 8.55 billion crowns ($1.08 billion).
Astra said it expected to increase market share for Losec to 45 percent from its current 35 percent in the United States.
But analysts, particularly disappointed by drop in operating profit to 6.75 billion crowns ($849 million) from 6.30 billion crowns ($792 million), said Astra faced an uphill battle.

"They face an enormous challenge, given the size of Losec, and I think they will continue to struggle and underperform the sector in terms of sales and earnings," said analyst Jan Dworsky from CI Nordic Securities.
"We are negative on the stock and will continue to be so for some time," Dworsky said.
"The Astra story is starting to look more and more suspect," Dresdner Kleinwort Benson analyst Steve Putnam said.
"The numbers were a bit disappointing ... especially as people were expecting to see a rebound from a weak first quarter that was affected by stockpiling in late 1996," Putnam said.
Astra said its North America sales rose to 6.33 billion crowns ($796 million) from 4.81 billion crowns ($605 million), which, calculated at constant rates, was a rise of 18 percent.
